items.title: Persist an exact RED for TEST-transition fresh-PASS reuse
items.context: Convert the isolated reproduction into a production-path test using the real local CLI sequence. It must prove current code reaches commandExecutions=0 yet returns infra_failure solely because trusted lifecycle metadata is dirty; retain a negative control for pre-existing human/external dirt.

happy.desc: A production-path regression harness drives the local worktree CLI through a real REVIEW-to-TEST story_advance followed immediately by mandatory validate, without an intervening git add/commit, and on the current implementation proves validation selected the fresh PASS (disposition reused, commandExecutions=0) but returned infra_failure solely with canonical-pass-persistence-failed naming lifecycle-generated process-events metadata; the harness is committed while still RED before the production fix.

edge.desc: The RED fixture isolates counters and scratch artifacts outside the fixture repository and asserts no configured validation command executed, so repository pollution by the harness cannot masquerade as the product failure.

The fixture records the exact pre-validate git status and the post-failure dirty rows, demonstrating the offending managed metadata was absent on command entry and was created by the authorized TEST transition rather than pre-existing dirt.

adversarial.desc: A negative control with a pre-existing direct or human-authored managed-metadata modification is refused before reuse persistence and is never reclassified as trusted merely because its path or event type resembles canonical lifecycle output.

The regression fails if the product invokes any full validation command, silently commits arbitrary dirt, or reports PASS despite a persistence failure; only the exact zero-command infra_failure signature qualifies as the intended pre-fix RED.

items.userSees: The RED terminal prints "status=fail", "failureKind=infra_failure", "canonical-pass-persistence-failed", and "commandExecutions=0" for the current implementation.

verificationEvidence.note: Commit 1f66c4c749 persisted the production REVIEW→TEST→validate RED and printed status=fail, failureKind=infra_failure, canonical-pass-persistence-failed, commandExecutions=0 before the fix.
The fixture keeps its counter under the OS temp directory and asserts the project-command count stays at one.
The fixture asserts a clean canonical baseline before transition and inspects exact post-transition canonical status.
Human-authored and forged codex_cli process-event deltas remain byte-identical after fail-closed rejection.
The RED/green fixture independently counts commands and rejects any hidden execution or false PASS.

items.title: Make trusted lifecycle metadata and reused PASS persist atomically
items.context: Differentiate canonical metadata created by the immediately preceding authorized lifecycle flow from pre-existing or untrusted dirt, and include only admissible generated paths in the isolated CAS/closeout writer transaction. Never allow arbitrary dirty files or prose/event-type spoofing to become trusted.

happy.desc: The authorized TEST transition snapshots a clean entry baseline, emits its own canonical phase/process-metrics metadata, verifies the exact post-write delta against that baseline, and atomically closes only those transition-generated files before returning; the subsequent verifier starts from a clean tree and independently persists the fresh reused PASS with disposition reused and commandExecutions=0.

The admission boundary is transition-local and causal: the transition proves exactly what it generated from its entry baseline and closes only that delta. The verifier receives no receipt or generalized permission to accept dirty metadata; any dirt present when validate begins, including canonical-looking event prose or allowed-path content, remains untrusted and rejected.

edge.desc: An authorized lifecycle invocation that produces no admissible metadata still reuses normally, while one that produces a strict subset or multiple canonical rows admits only the causally proven exact paths and leaves no partial transaction state.

The transaction rechecks HEAD, managed-path delta and proof freshness immediately before persistence; any concurrent HEAD or content movement aborts without writing a PASS receipt or committing another writer’s changes.

A closeout/CAS writer error or interrupted commit rolls back or leaves a classified recoverable failure with no false PASS, no partially staged/committed trusted metadata and no lost pre-existing user changes.

adversarial.desc: Direct edits, pre-existing human_confirmation rows, forged event-shaped JSON, copied/replayed canonical receipts, wrong-story or wrong-HEAD proofs, malformed/truncated receipts, path aliases and unproven additional managed files remain inadmissible even when their text and paths imitate an authorized lifecycle writer.

Source, configuration, command-entry, hook, untracked, symlink-resolved or unrelated dirty paths can never join the metadata transaction; detection fails closed to execution/refusal rather than laundering them into a reused PASS.

items.userSees: The first mandatory TEST validate prints "Validation PASS reused", "disposition=reused", and "commandExecutions=0" without requiring a metadata commit or retry.

verificationEvidence.note: Real TEST transition captures and atomically closes its exact index/process-events/process-metrics changed subset; immediate validate is reused PASS.
Verifier dirty rejection is unchanged; lifecycle and CLI writers use clean-baseline exact-path transactions only.
Transaction derives the strict changed subset from baseline while verifying hashes for the entire bounded path set.
Captured HEAD is rechecked and immutable metadata commit uses old-HEAD CAS.
Existing isolated writer hook/CAS/receipt failures restore managed index/worktree state and never publish PASS.
Direct human_confirmation and forged canonical-looking codex_cli rows are rejected without rewrite or commit.
Exact transaction path sets are derived from writer kind and story path; unrelated staged/source mutations remain outside commits.

items.title: Verify one-shot convergence and fail-closed security boundaries
items.context: The real TEST transition followed by mandatory validate must return PASS, disposition reused and commandExecutions=0 in one invocation with a clean tree. Human confirmation, forged event, malformed receipt, unrelated dirty source/config, concurrent HEAD change and writer failure must remain rejected or roll back safely.

happy.desc: From a clean fixture with a fully bound fresh PASS, the real local CLI performs story_advance into TEST and the immediately following mandatory validate succeeds in that single invocation with status PASS, disposition reused, commandExecutions=0, no canonical-pass-persistence-failed diagnostic and a clean final worktree.

Both human-readable and JSON output explicitly distinguish the successful reused path from executed, skipped, timed-out and failed validation, and the resulting fresh evidence remains bound to the current story/material/command-set identity.

edge.desc: Repeating validate after the one-shot convergence is idempotent: it remains a zero-command reused PASS, does not duplicate lifecycle facts or receipts, and leaves HEAD/worktree stable except for explicitly canonical idempotent bookkeeping.

A stale or mismatched material hash, story-files hash, focus, ordered command-set hash, policy/binding or non-trusted HEAD lineage does not take the reuse shortcut and follows the existing execute-or-refuse behavior without fabricating PASS.

The integration suite proves the production entrypoint/worktree runtime is used and counts command executions independently, preventing a global/old CLI or mocked helper-only test from producing a false green.

adversarial.desc: A table-driven matrix rejects pre-entry human/direct edits, forged canonical-looking events, replayed wrong-invocation proofs, malformed/truncated receipts and unrelated source/config/command-entry dirt; every case asserts commandExecutions, exit classification, unchanged user content and absence of a new PASS receipt.

Deterministically injected concurrent HEAD/content movement between admission and CAS causes a classified infra failure or safe retry, never a reused PASS and never loss/commit of the competing change.

Injected staging, commit, persistence-hook and cleanup failures settle once, release locks/resources, preserve diagnostic causality, roll back framework-owned partial state where possible and never require or recommend an identical blind rerun as proof of success.

items.userSees: The focused terminal prints "validation-evidence-reuse smoke: PASS" and "done-prepare auto-closeout smoke: PASS", while negative controls print "canonical metadata was already dirty".

verificationEvidence.note: Production local CLI prints status=pass, disposition=reused, commandExecutions=0 immediately after REVIEW→TEST and leaves exact canonical paths clean.
JSON and terminal log distinguish reused zero-command PASS and retain current identity/evidence bindings.
A second unchanged validate is asserted reused with commandExecutions=0 and the external counter remains one.
Existing identity/material/story-files/focus/lineage refusal matrix remains green.
Fixture resolves cli.js from the built worktree and independently counts actual project command entry.
Human and forged codex_cli rows are byte-preserved and rejected; existing malformed receipt and unrelated dirt matrix remains green.
HEAD is checked against capture before immutable old-HEAD CAS; existing concurrent-head regression remains green.
Done-prepare human metadata fail-closed control, process-fact contract, build, and diff check all pass; writer failures use isolated rollback primitive.
